title: Small cost yields many bad inputs
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n\ge 300$, and let $p$ be a deterministic one-way protocol for indexing on $n$-bit inputs. If its cost is at most $\lfloor n/10\rfloor$, then at least $2^{n-1}$ inputs $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ are bad for $p$, meaning that no answer vector of $p$ has Hamming distance less than $n/4$ from $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic one-way protocol for indexing on $n$-bit inputs
The protocol cost is at most $\lfloor n/10\rfloor$
replaced:
If $n \ge 300$ and the deterministic one-way protocol $p$ for $\mathrm{IND}_n$ has cost at most
$\lfloor n/10 \rfloor$, then at least $2^{n-1}$ of the $2^n$ inputs $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ are bad
for $p$ (no answer vector of $p$ lies within Hamming distance $n/4$ of $x$).
